findings: Both games launched and terminated cleanly at the protected 118-second deadline; exit 0 is not graphics acceptance.
GoW reaches visually confirmed gameplay at 9 FPS. Page protection takes 22.542 seconds across 9,122,970 calls; GPU waits take 19.153 seconds. Inclusive/concurrent timings are not additive.

GoT draw/dispatch/submit last timestamps are approximately 34.3 seconds; after 60 seconds median GPU busy is 0%. Game:Main has 88.180 seconds CPU at the 110-second snapshot, dominated by sampled guest timestamp polling and the host fault path. This does not prove clock emulation caused the black screen.
No GPU fault is reported, but validation and GPU-work tracing were disabled in this performance run; empty gpu-work.log is not absence of GPU execution.
Both model restoration leases finish RESTORED. Peak total VRAM stays about 5.12 GiB for GoW and 1.60 GiB for GoT; no prior-sized reload spike appears.
next_step: Reuse exact successful native binary for GoT-only Vulkan validation and bounded GPU-work capture, 118s TERM +2s KILL, no automated input. No new gameplay build or speculative emulation change.

findings: Black output with a small loading indicator at 80/110 seconds; both PNGs are byte-identical. Host overlay FPS does not show game progress.
Last recorded draw is at 32.157s and submission at 32.163s. These are recorded operations, not evidence of GPU completion. The work ring retains only 2048 of 227050 entries.
Vulkan validation is active and reports no IDs/errors. No GPU failure or memory fault is recorded. Absence of validation errors does not establish correct emulation.
Game:Main runtime grows from 59.401332532s to 89.138845025s between 80s and 110s, while GpuComm remains approximately 7.5247s and sleeps in futex. The exact condition and causal fault remain unknown.
No waiting shader hash or GPU timeout is identified. Raw guest shader bytes are retained only in the private evidence archive, not added to GitHub.

The prior performance capture showed timestamp polling and its host fault path, but it did not capture the pointed-to wait data or live thread stacks. CPU-ID/timestamps and shader semantics are unchanged.

findings: The PR174 collector succeeds natively in approximately 54ms per snapshot; it captures 5252 and 6756 profiler samples without exceeding capacity.
GoT remains black; the 80s and 110s PNGs are byte-identical. The host 29 FPS overlay is not game progress.

At both snapshots the main thread executes the same guest timestamp-delay loop and checks a 32-bit value at r13+4 which remains 1. This is consistent with waiting for outstanding work, but the object semantics and missing producer are unproven.

All ten job workers are sleeping with unchanged CPU runtime across the late snapshots. Seven captured worker stacks group into two shared condition-variable contexts. GpuComm is asleep too; no GPU fault is reported.

The hottest-eight policy excludes the movie decoder, GPU interrupt thread and some workers. The missing queue contents prevent distinguishing a lost notification from an empty queue or a blocked producer.
The protected stop requires SIGKILL after SIGTERM. The owned child is confirmed terminated, but its exit is -9, not a clean application exit. Shutdown profiler counters were consequently absent.
Vulkan validation is disabled for this performance capture; the preceding validation run had no errors. No emulation defect is established by these observations alone.
